facts: The appellants are original accused Nos. 2 and 3 in the said criminal proceedings.

M/s. Karl Logistics (for short 'said Company'), a company registered under the provisions of Companies Act, 1956 and is engaged in the business of logistics and iron ore supply and equipped with all necessary approvals and registrations for doing the business.

According to the terms, it was agreed that M/s. Platinum Buildcon will invest an amount of Rs. 1.50 crores with M/s. Karl Logistics for period of one month and would be entitled to profit of Rs.90 lakhs in addition to its investment of 1.50 crores or Rs.200 per tonne whichever is maximum.
Respondent No. 2 deposited the amount with M/s. Consistent in several instalments.
The appellants as well as respondent No. 2 filed the petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C.) for quashing of FIR.

It was agreed that respondent No. 2 would be entitled to withdraw the deposited amount of Rs.87 lakhs along with interest accrued thereon and, in addition, the appellants would also pay a further sum of Rs.5 lakhs.
issues: Whether the High Court should have exercised its discretion in quashing the proceedings.
What are the guiding factors in exercising the power under Section 482 of the Code?
Can the High Court quash criminal proceedings merely on the basis of compromise between the victim and the offender?
petitioner_arguments: The matter is settled by the complainant out of his free will.
In a case like this, where the proceedings are still at initial and nascent stage, the High Court should have exercised its discretion in quashing the proceedings.

The parties have reached the settlement and on that basis petition for quashing the criminal proceedings is filed, the guiding factor in such cases would be to secure: (i) ends of justice, or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any court.
respondent_arguments: There was no positive response received as per the MoU.
The appellants and original accused No.1/Mr. Birajdar has committed fraud.
The High Court should not have quashed the FIR merely on the basis of compromise between the victim and the offender.
court_reasoning: The power conferred under Section 482 of the Code is to be distinguished from the power which lies in the Court to compound the offences under Section 320 of the Code.

When the parties have reached the settlement and on that basis petition for quashing the criminal proceedings is filed, the guiding factor in such cases would be to secure: (i) ends of justice, or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any court.
The High Court should exercise its powers sparingly and with caution.
holding: The matter is settled by the complainant out of his free will.
The High Court should have exercised its discretion in quashing the proceedings.
The FIR lodged by respondent No.2 against the appellants is to be quashed.
